feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the positioning is clear, experience progression is logical, and the content shows real ownership of platforms, governance, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would be stronger with more quantified outcomes, less repetition across skills sections, and tighter formatting consistency.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression consistently support “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”  
- Good credibility: major platform scope, leadership responsibilities, and concrete tools/platforms (Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, etc.) make the profile believable.  
- Strong relevance and breadth: combines strategy, technical execution, governance, analytics, and content operations in a way that fits complex mission-driven organizations.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable results beyond scope metrics: include outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is weak/irrelevant filler; title casing is inconsistent (“Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” “Second Page Rail”). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors otherwise.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. It would be stronger with one or two concrete scale signals.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add measurable scope to sharpen impact, e.g. “10,000+ page platforms,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the list of capabilities to emphasize the most differentiating strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Replace “behind high-volume public-sector communications” with more direct outcome-oriented phrasing.
- Possible rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing public-sector web and communications platforms at enterprise scale. Leads website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; consider narrowing to “AI-enabled discovery” or “search.”
- “Digital leader” is close to the subtitle; the intro should add scale/results rather than restate positioning.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-level leadership capabilities will make it feel more distinct and executive-level.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and trim wording: “Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight systems • Multichannel communications leadership”
- Replace generic terms with stronger, broader labels: “AI-enabled search and content discovery” instead of “content experiences”; “Automation and platform integration” instead of “workflow automation and platform integration”
- Consider a more senior framing for the final items: “Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations”
- If space allows, reorder by strategic importance and recency: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation, multichannel operations, advocacy, multimedia

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled search” repeat language already used in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats accomplishments already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Emphasize scope, audience, or result where possible: e.g., “for county officials,” “to support campaign growth,” or “to improve policy-content discovery.”
- Standardize style and punctuation; use consistent verb-led phrasing and spell out “10 x 20-foot” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider this tighter version: “Selected Recent Projects: AI Hybrid Search—Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat. We Are Counties Microsite—Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10 x 20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video program spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats frequently; vary verbs or use a label-plus-description format.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact consulting entry. Tighten it around strategic outcomes and distinguish it from the prior NACo staff roles by emphasizing advisory scope, platform modernization, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web modernization, and content operations for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 outcome-focused points; e.g., combine digital systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one bullet.
- Add measurable scope where possible: number of sites/properties supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, user base, or efficiency gains.
- Rewrite for impact: “Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience” and “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components for scalable member communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 NACo role on governance, analytics, and digital operations.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless tied to a specific business result.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/operational leadership, and distinguish strategic ownership from the more execution-focused NACo roles below it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national membership organization.”
- Combine channel bullets and add outcomes: quantify email performance, social growth/engagement, video output, budget size, team size, or efficiency gains if available.
- Rewrite the website bullet to foreground transformation: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make governance/analytics results more concrete: note faster reporting, improved publishing consistency, reduced bottlenecks, stronger adoption, or better decision-making cadence.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Video leadership overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; here, focus on building the in-house studio and scaling capacity, not recurring video production.
- Governance/editorial workflow language overlaps with the current consultant role; keep this entry centered on enterprise ownership and transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Emphasize what changed under your ownership: scale, recurring programs, and cross-team operating improvements.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting coordinated advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and durable: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Reframe workflow/editorial bullets into one stronger line: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap; combine them.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the later Director of Digital Media role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the candidate’s senior-level positioning and reflect the most recent enterprise/public-sector leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with tighter, higher-signal wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider dropping “content leadership” from the title if the bullets already show leadership; e.g., “Digital Strategy & Governance.”
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing abstract concepts (“leadership”) with activities (“planning”).
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the title or nearby summary instead of here (e.g., 10,000+ pages, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with multiple NACo role bullets; keep this section more distilled than repetitive.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a tool dump rather than a senior, impact-oriented topline summary. For this section, emphasize platforms and modernization themes most tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from exhaustive list to a tighter leadership-oriented line, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Consider dropping jQuery unless it is actively used in recent roles; it dates the profile and adds little at topline level.
- Prioritize Drupal and CMS modernization first, since they align most clearly with the recent 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-linked: “AI-enabled search and discovery experiences for complex policy content”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, Airtable, and API integrations already appear in “Technical + IT”; repeating all of them here is redundant.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a tool list rather than a value statement. It also overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section, so this version should emphasize strategic application over platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboarding & optimization.”
- Use grouped language: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity” rather than separate bullets.
- Replace generic terms with outcome-oriented ones: “KPI framework development,” “executive reporting,” “SEO and digital performance analysis,” “insight generation for decision-making.”
- Suggested rewrite: “- Analytics strategy and reporting infrastructure - GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity - KPI framework development and executive dashboarding - SEO, user behavior and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current item duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for clarity and seniority.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production environment, delivery formats, and operational scope rather than broad labels.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic nouns with sharper, resume-style terms: “Broadcast-quality video production & post-production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio system operation.”
- Add scope or level where possible, e.g., “in-house studio production,” “recurring advocacy programming,” or “virtual, hybrid, and live event support.”
- Tighten to 4 concise bullets and align wording with recent experience:
- Broadcast-quality video production & editing
- Livestream, hybrid & virtual event production
- PTZ camera systems & studio operations
- Recurring advocacy and event media delivery
- If you can support it elsewhere, consider a stronger final bullet such as “In-house studio buildout and multimedia workflow design.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies.
- “Video production” and “studio” are already evidenced in recent NACo roles, so avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider trimming lower-signal tools if space is tight: Drupal • SharePoint • WordPress • Power Pages.
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal 10,” “enterprise SharePoint,” or “static site publishing via GitHub Pages.”
- Keep punctuation consistent and avoid overloading this line with tools better covered under coding/automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages” already appears in Topline Skills; repeating the exact list weakens both sections.
- GitHub Pages may feel too tactical unless supported elsewhere; consider removing if it was not material in recent roles.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group them more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI workflows**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; **HTML/CSS** is cleaner.
- If accurate, add a light impact cue tied to recent work, e.g. **“for Drupal microsites, analytics deployments and workflow automation”** in a short parenthetical or section intro.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations,” “Workflow automation”).
- **Google Tag Manager** may fit better under **Data, Analytics & Optimization** if you want this item to stay purely development-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and mixes automation platforms with project/collaboration tools. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere, so it should be tighter and more role-relevant.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/most relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams**
- Remove lower-value or older tools unless actively used recently: **Basecamp, Trello**
- If space allows, add light functional framing instead of a raw list: **Workflow automation, intake tracking, editorial planning, and cross-team coordination using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Microsoft Teams**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating all three with identical wording.
- Jira/Asana/Basecamp/Trello are similar category signals; listing all four can read as padding.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and misses the scale or type of email/engagement work you led. Because email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this line should stay concise and platform-focused.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show applied use: **Email campaign automation, newsletter operations, and audience engagement**
- Only keep platforms you used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/newsletter leadership is already covered in Work Experience, so avoid adding outcome claims here unless they are platform-specific
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader multi-channel communications language elsewhere; keep this item strictly tool-based

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely repeats the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the Director role. Make it more capability-led and slightly more senior by emphasizing implementation and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • reporting dashboards • SEO analysis • experimentation**
- Replace vague terms like **Dashboarding** with **reporting dashboards** or **executive reporting**.
- Swap **A/B testing** for **experimentation** only if you’ve actually led test design/analysis; otherwise keep **A/B testing**.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recent tools first: **GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item closely duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this version more tool-specific only.
- Avoid repeating analytics platform names elsewhere unless tied to a measurable outcome in recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any metrics you can recover.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs/results where possible: website refresh scope, number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten the close to show supervision without overstating management: “Mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- Possible version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported web, email, social and multimedia operations; contributed to a major website refresh; produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates; and improved day-to-day publishing workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with later governance/operations entries; keep this version more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Helped produce digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes, audiences served, cross-team partners, or types of research/projects supported.
- Keep this item concise so later, more senior digital leadership roles carry the narrative weight.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” is broad and repeats themes covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Avoid overemphasizing general communications work here; save space for the podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with stronger, higher-level multimedia claims elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize tools only, and keep workflow/production capabilities in the more strategic skills or experience sections.

Suggested edit:
